title: 1973 AHSME Problem 21
statement: The number of sets of two or more consecutive positive integers whose sum is \(100\) is

solutions.text:
For \(k\ge2\) consecutive positive integers starting at \(a,\) \[ 200=k(2a+k-1). \] Positivity gives \(k\lt\sqrt{200},\) so the possible divisors \(k\) of \(200\) are \[ 2,4,5,8,10. \] From \[ 2a=\frac{200}{k}-k+1, \] only \(k=5\) and \(k=8\) give positive even right-hand sides. They yield the sets \(18,19,20,21,22\) and \(9,10,\ldots,16.\) Hence there are \(2\) sets.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: If there are \(k\) terms beginning with \(a,\) double the sum to obtain \(200=k(2a+k-1)\)
Check divisors \(k\lt\sqrt{200}\) and enforce that \(a\) is a positive integer
